newsitem.title: USA: Aetna to restructure, cut 4,400 jobs, take charges.
newsitem.headline: Aetna to restructure, cut 4,400 jobs, take charges.

text.p: Aetna Inc. said Thursday it would restructure its health care and retirement services units, eliminate 4,400 jobs and take charges totalling $307 million.

Aetna, which earlier this year bought health maintenance organisation U.S. Healthcare, said it would take after-tax restructuring charges of about $32 million against its third-quarter earnings and an after-tax restructuring charge of about $275 million in the fourth quarter.
Analysts said the moves were critical for making Aetna's $8.9 billion merger with U.S. Healthcare a success.
"This is a necessary move," said Mark Puccia, director of insurance rating services at Standard & Poor's. "It was absolutely critical that they take this move to make the combination work."
Analysts said that for the newly merged company to succeed, Aetna must expand managed care expertise from its new U.S. Healthcare Corp. unit beyond the Northeast.

"What they have to do is show the world that they can integrate U.S. Healthcare and Aetna," said Todd Richter, an analyst with Dean Witter. "They have to show the world that, now that they've gone through this long process, they picked the right people."
Aetna said the third-quarter charges will cover severance and other costs in its Aetna Retirement Services unit, where a total of 400 jobs are to be cut by the end of the first quarter of 1998.
The fourth-quarter charges will cover $68 million for asset write-offs and $168 million in severance costs for Aetna U.S. Healthcare, where 4,000 job cuts are to be completed by the end of 1998.

Aetna said it would eliminate a total of about 7,500 positions in the unit, but that job growth is expected in some areas, such as sales and marketing. In addition, it said the regional consolidation of service centres and other functions will require a workforce reduction in some locations and the addition of jobs in others.
Aetna said it had about 23,000 employees in its healthcare business before the merger and U.S. Healthcare had about 5,000. Aetna now has a total of about 33,700 employees.
Most of the layoffs will come from the ranks of the Aetna employees, an Aetna spokeswoman said.
Despite the magnitude of the layoffs, Standard & Poor's Puccia said he was not concerned that Aetna had gone too far.
"We don't think they're cutting out muscle along with the fat," he said. "This is a level they can support."
Although Aetna was expected to cut jobs to eliminate duplication, it also was expected to cut other jobs as part of a strategic retooling of the two companies, analysts said.
"It goes beyond just eliminating the duplication," one source said.

The company said the moves announced Thursday were in line with its previously announced target of $140 million in administrative cost cuts. It said this would put Aetna U.S. Healthcare well on the way to achieving the previously announced target of $300 million of total cost cuts plus new revenues within 18 months from closing of the merger.
Aetna said it expects to report third-quarter results on Oct. 25.
Puccia said part of the cost cuts are expected to come as Aetna negotiates new, more favourable contracts with its healthcare providers comparable to those at U.S. Healthcare.
"They are aggressively going out and recontracting with their providers," he said.
In addition, Aetna hopes to generate new revenue by selling its traditional non-medical products, such as group life, dental and disability insurance, to the former U.S. Healthcare customers.
Aetna's stock lost $1 to end at $66.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.
